No corporate website could be reached for this operator this session, and no independent secondary source describing this specific facility was found, so address, capacity, and square footage remain not published in this record. Cyxtera Technologies, headquartered in Coral Gables, Florida, entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement with Brookfield Infrastructure, disclosed via an SEC Form 8-K titled "Cyxtera x Brookfield APA Press Release" and filed November 2, 2023, per SEC EDGAR's full-text search index; this registry has not independently confirmed the full scope of that transaction (whether it covered Cyxtera's entire US colocation portfolio or a subset) beyond the filing's existence. Separately, Cologix, a different operator tracked elsewhere in this registry, acquired two specific Cyxtera facilities, VAN5 in Vancouver and MTL12 in Montreal, in 2023, per Cologix's own materials; those two Canadian facilities are unrelated to this Florida facility and to the Brookfield transaction. Cyxtera's own public website resolves but displays content that reads as dated (referencing a 2017 executive appointment) with no current facility locations list, and its data-centers subpage returns a certificate error, a combination consistent with a company mid-transition following the Brookfield transaction rather than one actively maintaining public marketing infrastructure. No square footage, MW capacity, or current operational status specific to this Tampa facility was located in sourcing reachable this session. Fresh research this session, using web search tools unavailable in the prior exhausted pass, confirms this reverse geocoded address as the TPA1-A building, a 99,000 square foot facility with 6.3 megawatts of combined leased and available IT capacity per DataCenterHawk. Cyxtera itself filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2023 after operating more than 60 facilities totaling over 245 megawatts across 29 global markets; Brookfield Infrastructure Partners and institutional partners agreed to acquire seven of Cyxteras US data centers for 775 million dollars, including this Tampa property, in a deal that closed in early 2024 and merged Cyxteras retained facilities with Brookfields existing Evoque colocation platform into a combined operator later rebranded Centersquare, with over 330 megawatts of combined North American capacity.

reading:
Cyxtera is the earliest of three brand names this registry carries for one underlying colocation platform, and the row is kept rather than merged so that the buildings recorded under the old name stay findable. Cyxtera Technologies was assembled in 2017 from CenturyLink data centre assets, filed for Chapter 11 in June 2023, and Brookfield Infrastructure agreed in November 2023 to buy substantially all of its data centre assets for $775 million, closing in early 2024. Brookfield already owned Evoque, built from the AT&T data centre portfolio it bought in late 2018 for about $1.1 billion. In April 2024 Brookfield announced it was combining the two under a new brand, Centersquare, headquartered in Dallas, with Udhay Mathialagan as chairman and Spencer Mullee as chief executive. Trade coverage at the time described a combined platform of roughly 320 megawatts across more than 50 locations in 17 markets, with about 100 megawatts of near term expansion capacity. The company has since rebranded again as Csquare and went public in 2026. The canonical corporate profile lives on the Csquare row, uid d01580f9, with the intermediate Centersquare brand at uid fe5f655b.

Three buildings are recorded here. Cyxtera Tampa TP1 sits at 9310 Florida Palm Drive in Tampa, Florida. The successor operator's own Tampa specification sheet lists a site with 19,245 square feet of raised floor, 9 MW of utility power, 2.5 MW of UPS capacity, 9 MW of generator capacity and 11 service providers on net. Cyxtera Dallas-Fort Worth sits at 14950 Kingsport Road in Tarrant County, Texas, near the airport. The operator's Dallas-Fort Worth sheet lists a Fort Worth site with 133,298 square feet of raised floor, 51.9 MW of utility power, 16.4 MW of UPS, 24 MW of generator capacity, 14 providers on net and an NVIDIA DGX-Ready designation. The third is a five storey building at 1919 Park Avenue in Weehawken, New Jersey, tagged in the source data as the Cyxtera Citibank data centre. The operator's New Jersey sheet gives its Weehawken site as 300 John F. Kennedy Boulevard East with 199,110 square feet, 45.7 MW of utility power, 20.7 MW of UPS and 31 MW of generator capacity, and nothing published establishes whether the Park Avenue address is part of that same complex or a separate building.

Those numbers deserve care. Utility power is the service the building can draw. UPS capacity is the rating of the protected distribution. Generator capacity is standby diesel. None of the three is a stated critical IT load, and the operator publishes no IT load for any of these sites. Reconciling which of these three buildings also appear under the Centersquare and Csquare rows is left to facility level work rather than asserted here.
